title: Infrastructure as Code Foundations & Crossplane Control Planes
summary: Master modern Infrastructure as Code foundations: Kubernetes-native control planes with Crossplane, CompositeResourceDefinitions (XRDs), Compositions, application claims, and state drift reconciliation.
learningObjectives: Design declarative infrastructure control planes using Crossplane CompositeResourceDefinitions (XRDs).
Author reusable infrastructure Compositions binding managed cloud resources to developer claims.
Reconcile cloud resource state through declarative Kubernetes claims (e.g. PostgresInstance).

curriculumModules.title: Kubernetes-Native Control Planes vs Legacy IaC
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Traditional IaC engines run in point-in-time CLI pipelines, resulting in drift between runs. Crossplane transforms Kubernetes into a continuous infrastructure control plane, continuously reconciling cloud resources (AWS RDS, S3, VPC) against desired state via Kubernetes controllers.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Platform teams define CompositeResourceDefinitions (XRDs) encapsulating multi-resource blueprints; application teams consume simplified, self-service claims without needing direct cloud provider IAM credentials.

curriculumModules.title: Compositions & Developer Self-Service Claims
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Compositions translate an abstract claim (e.g. PostgresInstance) into concrete cloud resources (e.g. AWS rds.aws.upbound.io or GCP sql.gcp.upbound.io). Environment patching maps claim parameters into resource specifications.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce security guardrails in Compositions: mandatory encryption at rest, automated daily backups, multi-AZ high availability, and network isolation within private subnets.

labs.title: Defining a Crossplane CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD)
labs.scenario: Platform engineering requires a standard database specification. Author and deploy a Crossplane CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD) named xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io with group database.kubelabs.io, claimNames.kind PostgresInstance, and names.kind XPostgresInstance.
labs.productionContext: XRDs establish the platform API contract, defining custom resource schemas that application developers can provision without having cloud admin permissions.
objectives: Apply XRD to cluster and verify spec.claimNames.kind is PostgresInstance.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: CompositeResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io
spec:
  group: database.kubelabs.io
  names:
    kind: XPostgresInstance
    plural: xpostgresinstances
  claimNames:
    kind: PostgresInstance
    plural: postgresinstances
  versions:
    - name: v1alpha1
      served: true
      referenceable: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                parameters:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    storageGB:
                      type: integer

steps.title: Apply XRD to cluster
steps.instruction: Apply the XRD using kubectl and inspect the defined custom resource definition.

validationRules.name: xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io
validationRules.remediation: Apply XRD manifest with name xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io

validationRules.name: xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io
validationRules.remediation: Set spec.claimNames.kind: PostgresInstance in the XRD

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /iac/xrd-postgres.yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: CompositeResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: xpostgresqlinstances.database.kubelabs.io
spec:
  group: database.kubelabs.io
  names:
    kind: XPostgresInstance
    plural: xpostgresinstances
  claimNames:
    kind: PostgresInstance
    plural: postgresinstances
  versions:
    - name: v1alpha1
      served: true
      referenceable: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                parameters:
                  type: object
                  properties:
                    storageGB:
                      type: integer
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: XRD resource not found or claimNames.kind mismatch.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: The manifest omitted claimNames or was not applied.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Apply /iac/xrd-postgres.yaml and verify spec.claimNames.kind is PostgresInstance.

labs.title: Provisioning Cloud Resources with Developer Claims
labs.scenario: An application developer needs a dedicated managed database. Create namespace team-fintech and apply a PostgresInstance claim named fintech-payment-db with parameters.storageGB: 50. Run crossplane status to inspect the control plane reconciliation state.
labs.productionContext: Claims allow application teams to self-service cloud infrastructure using standard Kubernetes manifests, decoupling application delivery from cloud-specific APIs.
objectives: Deploy PostgresInstance fintech-payment-db in namespace team-fintech.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: database.kubelabs.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostgresInstance
metadata:
  name: fintech-payment-db
  namespace: team-fintech
spec:
  parameters:
    storageGB: 50

steps.title: Create namespace team-fintech
steps.instruction: Create the namespace for the fintech application team.

steps.title: Apply PostgresInstance claim
steps.instruction: Save and apply the PostgresInstance claim to namespace team-fintech.

steps.title: Inspect Crossplane control plane status
steps.instruction: Run crossplane status to verify control plane reconciliation.

validationRules.description: PostgresInstance fintech-payment-db exists in namespace team-fintech
validationRules.name: fintech-payment-db
validationRules.remediation: Apply PostgresInstance fintech-payment-db in namespace team-fintech

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /iac/claim-postgres.yaml
apiVersion: database.kubelabs.io/v1alpha1
kind: PostgresInstance
metadata:
  name: fintech-payment-db

    storageGB: 50
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: PostgresInstance not found in team-fintech namespace.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Namespace was not created or manifest was applied to default namespace.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary architectural difference between Crossplane and traditional CLI-based IaC tools like Terraform?
options: Crossplane cannot provision databases or storage buckets.

Crossplane operates as an active, continuous Kubernetes control plane running reconciliation loops that continuously detect and heal infrastructure drift, whereas traditional IaC executes only during episodic pipeline runs.
Terraform runs directly inside the Linux kernel via eBPF.
Crossplane requires writing infrastructure in C++ instead of YAML.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Crossplane leverages the Kubernetes controller pattern: it continuously polls cloud provider APIs, reconciling actual state with desired state declared in Kubernetes etcd, thereby autonomously healing drift.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Crossplane, what role does a CompositeResourceDefinition (XRD) play?
options: It defines the custom OpenAPI schema and kind for composite resources and claims, establishing the self-service API contract for developers.
It compiles HCL scripts into binary container images.
It configures CoreDNS upstream forwarding servers.
It replaces the Kubernetes kubelet daemon on worker nodes.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: An XRD defines the custom API type (schema, group, kind) that encapsulates one or more cloud resources. Application teams create lightweight claims matching the XRD contract without touching provider-specific resource definitions.
